item.title: Teenage boy dies in tractor crash in Co. Clare
item.description: A teenage boy has died after a crash involving a tractor in County Clare. The 16-year-old was driving the tractor when the collision happened shortly before 2pm yesterday. Gardaí are appealing for witnesses. Emergency services were called to the scene on the R458 at Bunnahow, north of Crusheen in County Clare, shortly before 2 o'clock yesterday afternoon. item.title: Today marks 53rd anniversary of Belturbet Bombing
item.description: Today marks the 53rd anniversary of the Belturbet bombing that caused the death of two young teenagers, Geraldine O'Reilly and Patrick Stanley. Geraldine who was 15 years of age and from the area and Patrick who was 16 years of age who was from Clara in Co Offaly lost their lives on the Main Street in Belturbet on this day 53 years ago. item.title: Appeal issued on anniversary of Belturbet Bombing
item.description: This day 53 years ago, on the 28th December 1972 a series of three no warning bombs exploded in Belturbet, Clones and Pettigo. The car bomb which exploded on Main Street, Belturbet killed two teenagers. At 10:28pm that night , 1972 a car bomb exploded outside Farrelly’s Bar and McGowan’s Drapery on Main Street, Belturbet. Two children, 16 year old Patrick Stanley and 15 year old Geraldine O’Reilly were killed instantly and eight more people were injured. Patrick Stanley (16) was from Clara, Co.

item.title: Samaritans urging locals to consider volunteering
item.description: Samaritans are urging locals to give something back to their community in the New Year and consider becoming a helpline volunteer. A new hub operated by Samaritans officially opened in recent weeks in Monaghan Town. The newly trained volunteers in Monaghan are answering calls to Samaritans' national freephone helpline, 116 123, which is open 24/7. item.title: Two churches broken into in Newtownhamilton
item.description: Police are appealing for information following the reports of two burglaries at churches in Newtownhamilton on Christmas Day, Thursday, 25th December. It was reported to police that sometime between 3.00pm on December 25th and 9.00 am on Friday, 26th December entry was gained to churches on Dundalk Street and Castleblayney Street in the town. Damage has been caused to both churches and a number of items have been taken including electronic speakers and a wall clock. Advertisement Sergeant Nelson
